sources.what_it_gave: Fazio -> Ariba -> servers -> POS -> NetBIOS share -> dump server -> FTP exfil

narrative_before: Attackers targeted Target's HVAC vendor Fazio Mechanical with phishing, compromising Fazio systems and stealing Active Directory credentials used with Target's Ariba external vendor portal (Senate report). Using the valid credentials they compromised additional servers (including via a BMC Software management default account) and moved laterally, then dropped tailored BlackPOS RAM-scraping malware (winxml.dll) onto point-of-sale systems. POS data was pushed over a temporary NetBIOS share to an internal dump server, which signalled a remote C2 server by ICMP, and was then exfiltrated to off-site FTP servers. The breach exposed ~40 million payment cards and ~70 million customer records.

detection_moments.description: Initial access into Target: stolen Fazio AD credentials used against the Ariba vendor portal.
detection_moments.evidence: 'Targeted third-party supplier to gain access to Target's internal systems ... Attackers compromised AD credentials ... Ariba System used by Fazio employees with AD credentials' - CTID flow / Senate report

detection_moments.description: Lateral movement to servers and POS systems; BlackPOS deployed; POS data staged to an internal dump server over a temporary NetBIOS share.
detection_moments.evidence: 'Attackers dropped malware to Target's POS systems ... An internal dump server is created to collect POS information from multiple systems via the temporary NetBIOS share' - CTID flow / Senate report

attack_path: valid accounts + BMC default account abused to expand into internal servers - T1078 / T1078.001
tailored BlackPOS RAM scraper dropped onto POS systems - T1105
POS data pushed over temporary NetBIOS share to internal dump server - T1074.002 / T1570
ambiguities: Many POS systems and 'additional servers' are not individually named; modelled as generic groups within the rule cap.
Off-site FTP exfiltration servers are external attacker infra, not modelled as victim machines.
Detection: Target's own alerts (FireEye) were reportedly not actioned; m2 marks the POS-staging stage first publicly known.
